Only methods declared in sugar-ansi-parser/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

SugarCraft\AnsiParser

AnsiTokenizer final class

Stream tokenizer for terminal output bytes: raw bytes in, a list of Token records out.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
parse(string $chunk): arrayTokenize $chunk. Returns the tokens that are complete now; an unfinished trailing sequence is held for the next call.
pendingBytes(): intNumber of bytes held from earlier parse() calls. Read-only: a caller that judges the cap on the whole buffer (held bytes plus the next chunk) needs the held length before it feeds the chunk.
flush(): arrayReturn any held partial sequence as one TEXT token and clear the buffer. Call at end of stream so a stuck partial comes back as text rather than disappearing.

Token final class

One classified slice of a byte stream, as emitted by AnsiTokenizer::parse().

paramInts(): arrayParse $params as a semicolon-separated list of integers (CSI convention). An empty slot reads as 0.

Dcs final class

Structured DCS decoder — the shared codec home for the sequence semantics a byte-stream inspector needs. The migration is landed: candy-ansi-inspect's Inspector::describeDcsParts() classifies through kind() and layers inspector-styled labels on top, while Inspector::describeDcs() survives only as a payload-string compatibility shim. Standing direction: new DCS sequence semantics belong here, consumed by the inspector — never hand-rolled a second time inside it.

MethodSummary
static parse(int $final, array $params = [], int $prefix = 0, int $intermediate = 0, string $data = ''): selfDecode one DCS dispatch.
final(): int
params(): array
prefix(): int
intermediate(): int
data(): string
isTruncated(): boolTrue when no final byte ever arrived (the final === 0 sentinel).
isSixel(): bool
kind(): stringOne of the KIND_* constants. The DECRQSS check runs before the sixel check because both share the final byte q — the $ intermediate is what separates the DECRQSS request from a DECSIXEL image.
describe(): stringOne-line, control-byte-safe summary. Payload bytes are attacker- controlled on an untrusted stream, so they are escaped rather than copied verbatim (same discipline as the inspector's label sanitizer).

Action enum

Cases: None · Clear · Collect · Prefix · Dispatch · Execute · Start · Put · Param · Print

BulkPrintHandler interface

Opt-in capability: receive contiguous printable-ASCII runs from the Ground fast path as ONE printRun() call instead of one Handler::printChar() per byte (finding sugar-ansi-parser-002).

MethodSummary
printRun(string $run): voidA maximal contiguous run (length >= 1) of printable-ASCII bytes (0x20-0x7E) collected while in Ground, arriving at exactly the point where the equivalent per-byte printChar() calls would have occurred.
printChar(string $rune): voidPrint a single codepoint (one UTF-8 rune) to the current cursor cell.
execute(int $byte): voidExecute a C0 or C1 control character (HT, LF, CR, BEL, BS, IND, RI, …).
csiDispatch(int $final, array $params, int $prefix, int $intermediate): voidDispatch a completed CSI sequence.
escDispatch(int $final, int $intermediate): voidDispatch a completed two-byte ESC sequence (e.g. ESC D = IND, ESC 7 = DECSC).
oscDispatch(string $data): voidDispatch a completed OSC sequence; data is everything between ESC ] and the terminator (BEL, ST, or ESC \).
dcsDispatch(int $final, array $params, int $prefix, int $intermediate, string $data): voidDispatch a completed DCS sequence.
sosPmApcDispatch(string $kind, string $data): voidDispatch a completed SOS, PM, or APC string.

CsiHandler interface

Receives CSI (Control Sequence Introducer) dispatches from the parser.

MethodSummary
printable(string $rune): voidPrint one character to the current cell.
cuu(int $count): voidCursor Up — move cursor up $count rows.
cud(int $count): voidCursor Down — move cursor down $count rows.
cuf(int $count): voidCursor Forward — move cursor right $count columns.
cub(int $count): voidCursor Back — move cursor left $count columns.
cup(int $row, int $col): voidCursor Position — move cursor to $row, $col (1-indexed).
hvp(int $row, int $col): voidHVP — Horizontal and Vertical Position. Move cursor to $row, $col (1-indexed). Semantically identical to CUP; kept as a distinct method because upstream treats CSI f and CSI H as separate control functions.
sgr(array $params): voidSelect Graphic Rendition — set text attributes from $params.
ed(int $mode): voidErase Display — clear screen regions.
el(int $mode): voidErase Line — clear line regions.
decset(int $mode, int $prefix): voidDECSET — DEC private mode set (prefix byte 0x3C-0x3F, e.g. '?').
decrst(int $mode, int $prefix): voidDECRST — DEC private mode reset.
decstbm(int $top, int $bottom): voidDECSTBM — set top and bottom scroll region margins.
tbc(int $mode): voidTBC — tab clear.
cht(int $count = 1): voidCHT — Cursor Horizontal Tab. Moves the cursor forward $count tab stops.
cbt(int $count = 1): voidCBT — Cursor Backward Tab. Moves the cursor back $count tab stops.
cr(): voidCR — carriage return. Move the cursor to column 0 (row unchanged).
lf(): voidLF — line feed. Advance the cursor down one row, scrolling the scroll region when already at the bottom margin.
su(int $count = 1): voidSU — Scroll Up (CSI S). Scroll the scroll region up $count lines, introducing blank lines at the bottom.
sd(int $count = 1): voidSD — Scroll Down (CSI T). Scroll the scroll region down $count lines, introducing blank lines at the top.
il(int $count = 1): voidIL — Insert Line (CSI L). Insert $count blank lines at the cursor row, shifting existing lines down within the scroll region.
dl(int $count = 1): voidDL — Delete Line (CSI M). Delete $count lines at the cursor row, shifting lines below up within the scroll region.
ich(int $count = 1): voidICH — Insert Character (CSI @). Insert $count blank cells at the cursor, shifting the rest of the line right.
dch(int $count = 1): voidDCH — Delete Character (CSI P). Delete $count cells at the cursor, shifting the rest of the line left.
rep(int $count = 1): voidREP — Repeat (CSI b). Repeat the last printed graphic character $count times.
scosc(): voidSCOSC — SCO Save Cursor (CSI s). Save the current cursor position.
scorc(): voidSCORC — SCO Restore Cursor (CSI u). Restore the saved cursor position.
gridRows(): intNumber of rows in the cell grid (used as bottom-margin default).
gridCols(): intNumber of columns in the cell grid.

__construct(private readonly CsiHandler $csi, private readonly OscHandler $osc, private readonly ?Handler $fallback = null)Construction-site note for finding sugar-ansi-parser-007: the three- argument shape is the safe one, but the $fallback stays optional for BC — built WITHOUT it the sieve's drops are silent, which is exactly the trap renderer bridges keep falling into.
static wired(CsiHandler $csi, OscHandler $osc, Handler $fallback): selfNamed constructor with a MANDATORY fallback — the compile-time refusal of the silent-drop shape (finding sugar-ansi-parser-007, arm a). The bare three-arg new remains for BC, but code that must observe the ESC family, DCS, SOS/PM/APC payloads, unmapped CSI finals and the non-routed executes can now say so at the call site instead of discovering the loss in a screenshot.
withFallback(Handler $fallback): selfA NEW adapter whose sieve-unconsumed events route to $fallback, sharing this one's csi/osc sides (finding sugar-ansi-parser-007, arm b). The swap constructs rather than mutates — the adapter is stateless — so $this keeps its existing fallback (or silence) untouched.

Parser final class

VT500 ANSI parser state machine.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly Handler $handler, private readonly bool $replaceMalformed = false, private readonly int $maxStringBuffer = self::MAX_STRING_BUFFER)
feed(string $bytes): voidFeed a chunk of bytes through the state machine. Safe to call repeatedly; in-flight sequences carry across calls.
parseComplete(string $bytes): voidFeed a complete byte sequence and guarantee end-of-stream flush.
flush(): voidForce any in-flight string sequence (OSC/DCS/SOS/PM/APC) to dispatch with whatever payload has been collected, and return to ground. Useful at end-of-stream.
reset(): voidReset the parser to ground state.
discard(): voidAbandon everything in flight WITHOUT dispatching: the anti-verb of reset().
subparams(): arrayECMA-48 sub-parameter continuation flags for the current (in-flight) or most recently dispatched CSI/DCS parameter list: true at index i means params[i] was followed by :, i.e. params[i + 1] belongs to the same parameter group. Indices beyond the last flag default to false — an empty result means the list held no : separators.
static groupSubparameters(array $params, array $flags): arrayReconstitute ECMA-48 parameter groups from a flattened params list plus the subparams() continuation flags: each group is one parameter followed by its :-separated sub-parameters. CSI 4 : 3 m yields [[4, 3]] (one underline-style parameter) while CSI 4 ; 3 m yields [[4], [3]] (underline, then a separate SGR 3) — the distinction the flat list alone cannot express.
stringOverflowed(): boolWhether the string payload of the sequence CURRENTLY BEING DISPATCHED was clipped by the maxStringBuffer cap (finding sugar-ansi-parser-013, sap-06). Both collection routes set it — the per-byte put() drop and the bulk sweep's clipped run.
